adapter: <scratch>/fresh/tardiness/repo/rsi6/environments/tardiness.py (manifest rsi6/environments/manifests/tardiness.json, data rsi6/data/tardiness/). OR-Library single-machine total weighted tardiness: wt40, wt50, wt100 (375 instances), references wtopt40, wtopt50, wtbest100b.
statement: The parsing, evaluation, scoring and relabelling are correct. I wrote my own parser from the pinned page wtinfo.html, and it reproduced every p, w and d array of all 375 instances and every reference value exactly. The manifest's eight SHA-256 hashes match the files on disk, and five files I downloaded again match too. The answer form (the n positions in index order, each job used once, no idle time) is the published problem without loss. My own evaluator agrees exactly with the adapter on 384 complete answers and on 72 partial states, with every candidate row checked. The zero point (the exact expected value of a uniformly random order) matches my own calculation by a different method to within 8e-15 on all 375 instances, and matches exact averages over all n! orders to within 3.4e-16 on 59 small cases. Nothing the learner sees changes when the references change. training=True and training=False give identical problems. The problem exposes only the file's p, w and d, with the jobs randomly relabelled. The code has no search, ranking or heuristic. Every malformed answer I tried scores 0. The weak point is the threshold. On the 24 fresh instances, simply taking the better of two sorting rules (by due date, or by w/p) already averages 0.908, above the 0.90 threshold. On the deciding half it averages 0.967: 9 of its 14 instances have reference 0, and sorting by due date reaches it exactly. The anchor quotes only the all-instance average of 0.89, so a reader would think these rules fall short of the threshold. A result of "capability held" here would therefore be misread. Three smaller problems: (1) the module text says the order of jobs in the files carries nothing, but wt100 lists every instance in exact w/p order (the relabelling removes this); (2) the category has no roles entry, so the kernel test module fails to load; (3) decode accepts negative labels, which only the kernel's validity check stops. One fresh class (TF 0.4, RDD 0.8) also appears in training at another size, which the work order's grouping allows. No twins or near-duplicates were found.
coverage:
Every script lives in <scratch>/fresh/tardiness/audit1 and was run as `cd audit1 && OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 nice -n 10 python3 -I <script>`. Because -I ignores PYTHONPATH, each script adds the package path itself and sets sys.dont_write_bytecode, so nothing was written under repo. A stub module stands in for rsi6.learner, so importing rsi6.kernel.run (used for halves, layout and _valid only) loaded no learner code. Total CPU was about 4 minutes, with no single run over 51 s.

Scripts: mine.py (my own parser and evaluator, a Gauss-Legendre zero point and a brute-force average), check_brute.py, dump.py, check_zero.py (run in chunks), check_main.py, check_order_priv.py, check_split_anchor.py, check_last.py, check_fresh.py, check_manifest.py. Downloads went into audit1/dl and were read as bytes only.

What was checked:
- I read every line of tardiness.py and its manifest.
- Data and references were compared on all 375 instances.
- The zero point was recomputed on all 375 instances by a method that shares nothing with the adapter's: random keys, an exact quadrature, prefix/suffix probability tables and a stop-loss transform, with no subset counts. It was also checked against exact Fraction averages over all n! orders, for n from 1 to 9.
- Generic kernel checks, without the learner: fast rows equal the specified rows exactly at every step of 8 instances; one layout across all 375; the view's public attributes; _valid on 10 malformed answers; relabelling differs per instance and per seed; repeated calls give byte-identical problems; the split keeps groups apart; assign and evaluate are charged to the meter.
- Privileged information: I built a second environment with every reference set to 0, and also patched references in place. Pickles, view arrays and full step-by-step greedy traces (every candidates() output, final totals, evaluate and decode) were compared on 30 instances × 3 seeds × 2 training flags, and the split was compared.
- I scanned the exposed numbers for each reference value (details under exposed).
- Order of jobs in the raw files: rank correlations with ties averaged, the score of the file order, and the score of the identity order after relabelling (3 run seeds × 375).
- Degenerate answers to score(): 15 kinds.
- Classes: for each of the 75 runs of five, whether the page's (TF, RDD) pair covers all five instances' due dates, and whether the share of zero due dates matches the share of each interval below zero.
- Twins: (p, w) matches at the same position, multiset overlaps and identical sorted p, over all pairs of instances.
- Anchor numbers, using my own evaluator and zero point: due-date order, w/p order, the better of the two, and an adjacent-swap descent from the better one. Also the excess over the reference at a score of 0.90, and the average score of random orders (1000 per instance).
- Manifest: hashes, five fresh downloads, the directory listing, and the legal page.

Not checked:
- The adapter's likelihood margins ("22.6 nats", "374 of 375"). My own rule found the page's pair consistent with every run but does not single it out in 66 of the 75 runs.
- The claim that the threshold was fixed before any answer was scored: the repository copy has no history.
- Whether run.measure itself needs a roles entry. I read only split, halves, layout and _valid, although my first read of run.py also showed lines 76-90 of measure.
- Learner-dependent tests (the learner's Layout names).
- Optimality of the references, which the rules exclude. A light sanity check found that no simple order goes below any reference.

findings.title: The 0.90 threshold is met on the fresh instances by the better of two sorting rules, and the anchor does not say so
findings.problem: The threshold is applied to the fresh instances of split(env, 16, 24) and their halves. On those 24 instances, the better of the due-date order and the w/p order already averages 0.908, above the threshold. On the deciding half A it averages 0.967, and on the confirming half B 0.826. An adjacent-swap descent from it averages 0.969 on the fresh side; over all 375 it averages 0.946 and reaches 0.90 on 81% of instances. 9 of the 24 fresh instances, all of them in half A (9 of its 14), have reference 0, and the due-date order reaches it exactly (score 1). The anchor and the module text quote only the all-instance average of 0.89, which sits below the threshold, so a reader concludes these rules fall short. A 'capability held' result here would be misread as more than choosing between two sorts.
findings.evidence: check_last.py printed: 'better of EDD and WSPT on fresh (24): mean 0.908', 'A (14): 0.967', 'B (10): 0.826', 'train (16): 0.893'. check_split_anchor.py printed: 'best2 mean score 0.887 share >= 0.90: 0.54 fresh-24 mean: 0.908' and 'api mean score 0.946 share >= 0.90: 0.81 fresh-24 mean: 0.969'. check_fresh.py printed: 'fresh: 24 instances, reference 0 on 9, EDD equals the reference on 9', 'A: 14 instances, reference 0 on 9', 'B: 10 instances, reference 0 on 0'. The all-instance numbers the anchor does state (0.51, 0.80, 0.89, 54%, median 23%, quartiles 13% and 72%) were confirmed.
findings.fix: Add to `anchor` and to the threshold paragraph of the module: 'on the 24 fresh instances of split(env, 16, 24) the better of the due-date order and the w/p order averages 0.908 (0.967 on the deciding half, 0.826 on the confirming half), and an adjacent-swap descent from it 0.969; 9 fresh instances (9 of the 14 of the deciding half) have reference 0, which the due-date order attains'. If 0.90 is meant to require more than these rules, then before any learner answer is scored, do one of two things and say so: raise the threshold above the descent baseline on the fresh side (for example 0.98, as an operating point), or leave out by an instance-only rule the 53 instances on which the non-decreasing due-date order has no tardiness. That rule reads no reference, and it is exactly the R = 0 set.

findings.title: Module text says the order of jobs in the files carries nothing; wt100 lists every instance in exact w/p order
findings.problem: The docstring says the jobs' order within an instance 'carries nothing: the generator drew them independently'. In wt100.txt, all 125 instances list their jobs in non-increasing w(j)/p(j) order, so the file order is the w/p sorting rule and scores 0.807 on average. In wt40 and wt50 the order shows no relation to p, w or d. Nothing reaches the learner: the relabelling is unconditional and removes the order, and the w/p order can be computed from the exposed attributes anyway. But the statement is false, and the protection rests entirely on the relabelling.
findings.evidence: check_split_anchor.py printed: 'instances listed exactly in WSPT order: 125' and 'n=100: rho(index, w/p) mean -1.000, min -1.000'; for n=40 and n=50 the mean is about 0. check_last.py printed: 'wt100: file (identity) order mean score 0.807; WSPT order 0.807; max |identity - WSPT| 0.00e+00'. check_order_priv.py printed: 'identity-in-new-labels mean score 0.065 (random orders: 0.068; file order: 0.322)'.
findings.fix: Replace '(their order within an instance carries nothing: the generator drew them independently)' with '(in wt100 the jobs of every instance are listed in non-increasing w(j)/p(j), the w/p order, which scores 0.81 on average; in wt40 and wt50 the order shows no relation to p, w or d; the relabelling removes the file order, and the w/p order is a function of the exposed attributes in any case)'.

findings.title: The category has no roles entry, so the kernel's test module fails at import
findings.problem: 'tardiness' is registered in rsi6/environments/__init__.py but is absent from rsi6/registry/roles.json. roles.role_of('tardiness') raises KeyError. test_kernel.py evaluates role_of at module level (ASSIGN_ENVIRONMENTS, lines 26-27) for every registered assign environment, so the module cannot be imported and none of the generic checks run with the standard command. test_problem_carries_no_reference and test_split_keeps_groups_apart would also raise.
findings.evidence: check_order_priv.py printed: "roles.role_of('tardiness') raises KeyError 'tardiness'". roles.json lists 16 categories, and tardiness is not among them.
findings.fix: In test_kernel.py, replace `roles.role_of(name)` with `roles.load()['roles'].get(name)` in ASSIGN_ENVIRONMENTS, test_problem_carries_no_reference and test_split_keeps_groups_apart. Alternatively, record the fresh categories' role in a registry the kernel reads, outside the drawn roles.json whose reproducibility is itself tested, before registering the adapter.

findings.title: decode accepts negative labels, so a malformed answer can decode to a valid order
findings.problem: decode returns perm[np.asarray(answer, dtype=np.int64)]. Numpy wraps negative indices, so labels -n..-1 (and floats, which are truncated) decode to a valid permutation, which score() then scores. Only the kernel's _valid, applied to the relabelled answer before decoding, prevents this. The same pattern appears in the earlier adapters.
findings.evidence: check_order_priv.py printed: 'decode of an EDD order written with labels -40..-1: _valid False | decode is a permutation True | score(decode) = 0.6996 | score of EDD itself 0.6996'.

evaluator_agreement:
- Own parser: matches the adapter's p, w and d arrays and all reference values (wtopt40, wtopt50, wtbest100b) on all 375 instances (0 mismatches); the adapter's reference() matches as a float.
- Complete answers: 384 on 6 instances (wt40-003, wt40-118, wt50-047, wt50-123, wt100-012, wt100-111). Of these, 360 are random orders built in relabelled problems with random seeds and then decoded; 24 are the due-date, w/p, file and reversed orders. evaluate() equals my own integer value on every one (0 mismatches). score() equals my own (Z - V)/(Z - R) cut to [0, 1], computed with my own Z and R, to within 4.8e-15.
- Partial states: 72 (random prefixes). totals() after assign() equals partial_totals() and my own prefix value exactly. Every candidate row equals both the difference of partial_totals() and my own increment w*max(t + p - d, 0); already-placed jobs give 0. The fast rows equal the generic slow rows exactly at every step of 8 whole instances.
- Zero point: within 8.0e-15 relative of my own calculation by a different method, on all 375 instances. It is within 3.4e-16 of exact Fraction averages over all n! orders on 59 small cases with n from 1 to 9 (both parities).
- Reference values: the extra statements also hold. wtbest100b is below wtbest100a at instances 111-114, 116 and 118-120, and above it nowhere. Reference 0 occurs 18, 17 and 18 times in the three files. The due-date order has no tardiness exactly on the 53 instances with reference 0. No simple order (due date, w/p, adjacent-swap descent) goes below any reference.
- Reference answers: the source publishes values only, with no processing orders, so whether the values are attained was not checked.
exposed:
- n_vars = n_opts = n (40, 50 or 100): the n positions of the processing order and the n jobs, from the page.
- ordered = True: the adapter's answer form. The page defines C(j) as the earliest completion time of a given processing order, so the order is the whole answer.
- capacity = ones(n): each job is processed exactly once (a processing order).
- hard = [False], detail = [False]: one soft group, Σ w(j)T(j), the page's objective; no constraints, and no detail group because the objective is a sum.
- opt_attr (n × 3) = [p(j), w(j), d(j)]: exactly the three numbers the file gives each job. Verified equal to my own parse with the rows permuted by decode's perm.
- var_attr: n × 0. var_var, opt_opt, var_opt, occ_attr: empty. domain, start_answer, start_totals: None.
- View: its public attributes are exactly the generic set, and the state keys are {a, n, tot, used}. The adapter's own p, w and d stay behind the view.
- Reference scan: the reference value appears among the problem's numbers on 60 instances. On 53 the reference is 0 and matches the 0.0 of the boolean hard/detail flags; on 7 a small R > 0 equals some p or w. All are coincidences: changing every reference to 0, or patching references in place, left the pickles, view arrays and full interaction traces byte-identical (0 of 180 environment pairs plus 30 in-place patches differ), and left the split unchanged. training=True and training=False give byte-identical problems on all 375. The generic test inspects only wt100-001, which does not collide.
- Design decisions that shape difficulty:
  - candidates() gives each remaining job's exact weighted tardiness if it went next. This is 0 for any job that would not be late, so it carries no slack information.
  - The zero point (a random order) sits far below simple rules: the due-date order scores 0.51, the w/p order 0.80, the better of the two 0.89.
  - The 53 instances with reference 0 are kept; the due-date order solves them exactly.
  - Groups are (n, TF, RDD), named by inference because the page does not say where each class sits in the files. They reach only the split, never the problem.
